title: Igulim and yosher: the dream that surrounds everything, and the deed that rules it
overview:
The *Kav* goes down from the *reshimu*, circles, goes down and circles again: the *igulim* are one line. In them the highest surrounds all and is best, and the innermost is lowest; in *yosher* it is the other way around. To see why, the chapter looks at the *ratzon kadum*, the original will. It is revealed compared to the *ratzon hamuchlat*, but still hidden and for oneself, like the stirring to have things your own way before you know it means a house, and it already holds every detail, down to the bathroom drapes. In the *Zohar*'s words it is *Atika d'Atikin*, and in the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, *Atika Stima'a*; the delight already in *chachma*, in *Atzilus*, is *Atika Kadisha*.

In the circles every cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it, as a kid's reasons never capture why he wants a bike. When the will comes to be done in actual fact, it reverses: will hides in intellect, intellect in *middos*, *middos* in the deed, and the *sof maaseh* becomes king. *Igulim* are *teshuva*, *yosher* good deeds. Of the Essence above the *Kav* nothing can be said: the *tzimtzum* is a jump, not a line.

terms.gloss: circles: the sefiros one inside the other, where the outermost, the will, is the main thing and everything inside is a token of it
the straight line: the sefiros enclothed one in the lower one in the shape of a person, where the deed is on the outside and on top
the original (not merely first) will: the origin of every detail, revealed compared to the ratzon hamuchlat but still hidden and for oneself
the final deed: in the circles the flimsiest daydream and the innermost; in yosher the top thing that everything has to fit
the Atik of all Atiks: the ratzon kadum as the inner pleasure behind all pleasure, the source of the pleasures in things outside oneself
the will of all wills: the same ratzon kadum, called by its will, since the taanug is the will inside the will
the hidden Atik: the Keser of Adam Kadmon, where the will is already associated with a thought; covered, but meant to be revealed
the most hidden of all hidden: the beginning of the Kav, which even the thought of Adam Kadmon cannot grasp
the holy Atik: the delight already in chachma, in a particular form; Atik Yomin and Arich Anpin of Atzilus
the bribe: the will makes the intellect biased, so it finds reasons to fit
the short line: one little point of the essence that stands for all of it, the jump from the reshimu to the ratzon kadum
the impression left after the tzimtzum: every possible limited thing, His choices of style without seeing Him in them; still infinite

sections.title: Circles and the straight line: one line that goes down and circles
sections.summary: The chapter sets out to explain the details of the *Kav* as it is in *igulim* (circles). The beginning of the *Kav* goes down a little, circles, goes down and circles again, so that the circles are really one line; in the circles the highest is the best and the innermost the lowest, and in *yosher* (the straight line) it is the other way around.

phrases.en: Now we have to start to understand

phrases.he: בפרטי ענין הקו כמו שהוא בבחינת עגולים כו'.
phrases.en: We have to understand how the *Kav* is already *igulim*

blocks.text: We just finished the *igulim* (circles) and the difference between the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will) and the *ratzon murkav* (the composite will). **Now we have to start to understand**, since until now we understood nothing, **how the Kav is already igulim.** *Yosher* (the straight line) is explained only in the next chapter; here he tells a little of it.

As explained, *igulim* is like the *ratzon* (will) for a house: the general *ratzon* divides into particular *ratzonos*, each like a circle. A circle includes everything inside it equally, one point holding it all, the way a context defines everything in it.

phrases.he: והנה תחלה יש להקדים בבחינת ראשית הקו הזה
phrases.en: So first we have to explain about the *reshis hakav*

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת אור פנימי ואחר כך מתעגל ונמשך בבחינת אור פנימי וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: first it comes down; the very first *hiyuli Kav* comes down from the *reshimu*, then it circles, and then it goes down and then it circles

blocks.text: **So first we have to explain about the reshis hakav** (the beginning of the line), before the *igulim*. The very first *hiyuli* (raw, general) *Kav* **comes down** from the *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*), **then it circles, and then it goes down and then it circles.**

blocks.title: Drawing it without lifting the pen
blocks.text: It looks like concentric circles with a line through them, but the circles are made of the line. Draw the picture without lifting your pen: down a centimeter, a circle back to the same point, down another centimeter, another circle, smaller and smaller. "It's really one line."

phrases.en: and it explains in *Etz Chaim*

phrases.he: שבבחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים, העליון מכולם משובח מכולם והפנימי מכולם גרוע כו',
phrases.en: the best one is on the outside, and the worst one, the lowest *sefira*, is on the inside

phrases.he: ובבחינת עשר ספירות דיושר להיפך, העליון גרוע והפנימי משובח כו'.

blocks.text:
**And it explains in Etz Chaim** that in the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* the highest is the best and the innermost the lowest, and in *yosher* the opposite.

In *igulim*, *Keser* (crown) is outside and *Malchus* (kingship) inside. In *yosher* each *sefira* is *mislabesh* (enclothed) in the one below: *Keser* in *Chabad*, *Chabad* in the *middos* (emotional attributes), the *middos* in thought, speech and action. So the outermost is *Malchus*, and inside it the *middos*, the intellect, the *ratzon* and the *taanug* (delight). Drawn, it is a question of which is outside.
Before talking about circles and lines, we have to understand what *igulim* and *yosher* mean at all.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum: a hidden first will for yourself that already holds every detail
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* (the original will) is revealed compared to the *ratzon hamuchlat*, but it is still hidden, a will for oneself, like the inner stirring to have things your own way before you know it means a house. It is the origin of every detail down to the last blade of grass, and the last deed, the end of the seventh millennium, was first in thought.

phrases.en: the explanation of these matters, these things

phrases.he: הנה ידוע שבחינת רצון קדום זה,
phrases.en: that this first *ratzon*, the *ratzon* for the house in the *mashal*

phrases.he: הגם שלגבי בחינת רצון הפשוט המוחלט בעצמות
phrases.en: even though compared to the *ratzon hamuchlat*
it's already called like a particular revealed *ratzon*
But the truth is, it's really still hidden
it's not revealed at all

phrases.he: כי אינו רק השפעת והמשכת רצון הפשוט של חפץ חסד שהוחלט בעצמות מכבר, כך יהיה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: All you know is that you want your *ratzon hamuchlat* to be revealed *b'poel mamash*

blocks.text: **The explanation of these matters**: **this first ratzon**, the *ratzon* for the house in the *mashal* (analogy), **even though compared to the ratzon hamuchlat, it's already called like a particular revealed ratzon**, since you went from a mere taste to wanting a house. **But the truth is, it's really still hidden; it's not revealed at all.**

With this first *ratzon* you do not yet know what you want; **all you know is that you want your ratzon hamuchlat to be revealed b'poel mamash** (in actual fact). A house you do not want until *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and not even a home before the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.title: Your parents are cramping your style
blocks.text: All there is, is an inner stirring, like the one people have at a certain age to be independent, to have their own space. You do not know what it is; you only feel that you do not like the way things are. Your parents are cramping your style: you want to go out, and it is wear a sweater, wash your hands. You just want things your way.

You do not yet know that this means your own house, job and life, still less what kind of house or where. It is the *ratzon* you have had since you were little, to have something of your own that expresses you: "this inner desire to like be yourself."

Wanting to be yourself sounds ridiculous, since you cannot not be yourself. What people mean by wanting to be, find or understand themselves is that they want to get the world to express them and fit them.

blocks.title: Getting the world to play your song
blocks.text: Like someone learning an instrument: he wants to get the world to play his song. He knows what he wants to play without realizing it, because he does not think in music. Certain things sound good to you, a *ratzon hamuchlat*, but you do not know the song until it comes out in the instrument: the *hiyuli* that has to come out. So the *ratzon kadum* is still hidden: you know what you want, but not tangibly.

phrases.he: ומיד שעולה במחשבה זאת שיהיה הכל,
phrases.en: as soon as it comes up in your thought, I want to do everything that was in my *ratzon hamuchlat*
that's called the first *machshava* and *ratzon*, or the original
which includes everything that's inside of it
all the particular desires inside of it
like we said about the *mashal* of the *ratzon* for a house

blocks.text: **As soon as it comes up in your thought** to do everything that was in the *ratzon hamuchlat*, **that's called the first machshava and ratzon, or the original**: the *machshava kduma* and *ratzon kadum*.

blocks.title: A father and a firstborn
blocks.text: *Kadum* means original, not first: the origin of everything else, which are its branches, while first just happens to come first. It is the difference between a father and a firstborn. The father is *kodem* to his children as their origin; the firstborn just happens to be first.

This original *ratzon* **includes everything that's inside of it, all the particular desires inside of it, like we said about the mashal of the ratzon for a house.** Say you want a house, and the other *ratzonos* are included. "The only reason that you want the kitchen sink is because you want a house": they rest on the general *ratzon* and are part of its definition.

phrases.he: אם כן עדיין רצון קדום זה הכל בעצמו
phrases.en: So, if so, this first *ratzon* is still totally within G-d Himself
it's not revealed yet outside, in anything separate
nevertheless, from it comes everything
afterwards
And this is what it says

phrases.he: כי הוא אמר, במחשבה הקדומה, ויהי כו'
phrases.en: that G-d said, and it was

blocks.text: **So this first ratzon is still totally within G-d Himself.** When a person first wants a home, he is thinking of nothing outside himself: he wants to feel a certain way, to express a style, a taste. **It's not revealed yet outside, in anything separate. Nevertheless, from it comes everything afterwards**, since everything is only its expression.

**And this is what it says**, "For He said," with the *machshava kduma*, "and it was": **G-d said, and it was.** *Amar* (said) always really means *machshava* (thought); even as speech, it is saying what is on your mind.

blocks.title: A proclamation and a chat with friends
blocks.text: An official proclamation is more than saying what is on your mind: the focus is on the *dibur* (speech) itself. Chatting with friends, the focus is on what you think, and a "you know what I mean" will do, because the words need not be exact. Focus on the thought behind the words is *amira*; focus on the words is *dibur*.

So "For He said, and it was" means He revealed Himself in a way of *machshava*, a *gilui* (revelation) of thought, here the *ratzon kadum*, the original thought. **G-d said** to Himself, deciding how He wanted the world to be, **and it was** all according to that. Once G-d told Himself, "I want a world, a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below)," everything else follows automatically as part of making it.

phrases.en: And this is called the life of all the worlds
from the beginning of *Adam Kadmon*
until the heel of *Adam Kadmon*
all the way down to the end of *Asiya*

phrases.he: והיינו כל היצור לא נכחד כו'
phrases.en: all of the formed things are not missing from You

phrases.he: שאין פרט היותר אחרון שלא קדם להיות ברצון ובמחשבה זו
phrases.en: There is nothing, not even the smallest detail, that escaped G-d's first *ratzon* and *machshava*; it was all there

blocks.text:
**And this is called the life of all the worlds**: the motivation behind everything is this one point, **from the beginning of Adam Kadmon** (explained next chapter) **until the heel of Adam Kadmon**, a general *partzuf* (stature) that goes **all the way down to the end of Asiya**.

This is what we say, "I think," in *Zichronos* on Rosh Hashana: **all of the formed things are not missing from You.** What does that mean?

**There is nothing, not even the smallest detail, that escaped G-d's first ratzon and machshava**, not the last hair on your head. Did G-d really think about how many hairs would be on my head? Yes. That is why everything is *hashgacha pratis* (individual Divine providence): G-d knows how many times a leaf will blow back and forth. And it is *noge'a* (relevant) to the whole purpose: for the *dira b'tachtonim* and *Moshiach*, the original *ratzon*, it has to be exactly so.

blocks.title: The bathroom drapes
blocks.text: Why should that matter? Think of wanting a house: the whole point is to have it exactly your way. Money is no object, and you get down to the bathroom drapes and the decorations. If one of those little things is off, you live there comfortably but do not have the original *ratzon*, that it is your space. So a rental whose landlord will not let you change the windows is not a real house.

blocks.title: The bathroom drapes
blocks.text: Such a little *prat* (detail), and if you cannot have it your way it takes away the whole thing: a good house, but no longer all yours. The bathroom drapes matter as much as the structure. "It's all or nothing deal."

So why must the grass blow exactly that way? Because G-d wanted it so, for whatever reason; that is what pleases Him, and with even one little thing off the whole thing is not worth it. "If a grass won't blow 7,296 times, what's it all worth?" One blade of grass would ruin everything, so it was all included in the first *ratzon kadum*.

blocks.title: Going out for pizza
blocks.text: Ask someone what he wants to do tonight and he says go out for pizza: that already has every detail, the *ratzon* to open the door included. All of it is covered.

phrases.en: On the contrary

phrases.he: סוף מעשה, כמו בסוף אלף הז', עלה במחשבה קדומה זו תחלה
phrases.en: the last thing was really the first in thought

blocks.text: **On the contrary**: the final deed, the end of the seventh millennium, came up first in this *machshava kduma*. The *ratzon* to chew the pizza was the first thought. So G-d's main *ratzon* was for the seventh millennium with all its little details, and we are getting closer to it.

These little details are the main things G-d wanted. Through history it becomes in a way less and in a way more. Adam and Avraham were the big movers, general people whose stories speak for all mankind; why is a story that happened to me the other day not recorded for all time? They have the advantage of being more general, higher in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent).

But the main *ratzon* was for when you go on *mivtzaim* (outreach campaigns) and put *tefillin* on someone, or learn a *maamar* (discourse). **The last thing was really the first in thought.** The wall structure is the least of your *ratzon hamuchlat* for a house: most people buy one and decorate and furnish it themselves. The big things are just functional; the biggest *gilui* of your *ratzon hamuchlat* is in the little things that serve no practical purpose and are just how you like it.

So the biggest *gilui* of G-d's *ratzon hamuchlat* is in the stupid little things that He wants the world for *Moshiach* *davka* (precisely) this way. He could have done it another way, but He likes it this way. Why are trees green and not brown leaves on green trunks? "Why does there have to be a bird-dropping spider? Nobody knows why." And there is room to say more about it.

sections.title: In the language of the Zohar: Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha
sections.summary: A parenthesis puts the *ratzon kadum* into the *Zohar*'s terms. In the *ratzon* there is a *taanug*, and they are one: as the source of all the pleasures and wills to come, in the *Kav* after the *tzimtzum*, it is *Atika d'Atikin*, the pleasure of all pleasures; enclothed in the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, already associated with a thought, it is *Atika Stima'a*, hidden but meant to be revealed; and as the pleasure already in a particular form, in *Atzilus*, it is *Atika Kadisha*.

phrases.en: in the words of the *Zohar*
the *ratzon kadum* is called the *Atik* of all *Atiks*, the inner pleasure behind all pleasure
or the hidden *Atik*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת רעוא דכל רעווין עילאין
phrases.en: This is also the *ratzon* of all upper *ratzonos*, the inner *ratzon*
which is revealed on the forehead of *Atika Kadisha*
because the *ratzon* inside the *ratzon* is the *taanug*
And they're really one thing

blocks.text: **In the words of the Zohar**: here he opens a kabbalistic parenthesis to put everything in context, translating the *Zohar*'s terms, for those used to them, into their mother tongue.

In the *Zohar*'s language **the ratzon kadum is called the Atik of all Atiks**, *Atika d'Atikin*, the inner pleasure behind all pleasure, **or the hidden Atik**, *Atika Stima'a*; the difference comes at the end of the parenthesis. **This is also the ratzon of all upper ratzonos**, *ra'ava d'chol ra'avin*, inner *taanug* and inner *ratzon* both, **revealed on the forehead of Atika Kadisha**, the *taanug* revealed in something particular.
Why both *Atika d'Atikin* and *ra'ava d'chol ra'avin*? **Because the ratzon inside the ratzon is the taanug. And they're really one thing**: call it *ratzon*, *ratzon kadum* or *taanug*, as you like.

phrases.he: וברצון הפשוט ההיולי שבחפץ חסד ההיולי (הנזכר לעיל באות יוד ואות יא) היה כלול בו התענוג
phrases.en: Even in the *hiyuli ratzon pashut* there was enclosed the *hiyuli taanug pashut*

phrases.he: הפשוט שבעצמות שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו כו'

phrases.en: in each of the three levels there's a *ratzon* and there's also the *taanug*
until it comes to a *prat*
that I'm going to be king

phrases.he: שזה בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: which is the *Malchus d'Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, which is the *ratzon hamuchlat* for our world

phrases.he: הכל בחינת שעשועי המלך בעצמו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: Those are all G-d's essential *taanug* in Himself

blocks.text: **Even in the hiyuli ratzon pashut**, the will of the *hiyuli chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness) of chapters 10 and 11, **there was enclosed the hiyuli taanug pashut**. And **in each of the three levels there's a ratzon and there's also the taanug, until it comes to a prat**, *Ana Emloch*, **that I'm going to be king**, the *ratzon hamuchlat* for our world. **Those are all G-d's essential taanug in Himself**: beside the *ratzon*, the pleasure He has in Himself.

phrases.en: but once you talk about *Atika d'Atikin*
which is the source of all pleasures, meaning pleasures you have in things separate from yourself
or the *ratzon* of all *ratzonos*
that's in the *Kav* that's after the *tzimtzum*
which is like one general *ratzon* or one general *taanug*, that you want to express yourself
that are going to come out *b'gilui*

blocks.text: **But once you talk about Atika d'Atikin, which is the source of all pleasures**, pleasures in things separate from yourself, it is **in the Kav that's after the tzimtzum**: **one general ratzon or one general taanug, that you want to express yourself.** It is the intermediary: before it, all enjoyment and *ratzon* is for yourself; after it, in things outside you. So it is the pleasure of all pleasures and the *ratzon* of all *ratzonos* **that are going to come out b'gilui** (in revelation).

phrases.he: ועתיקא סתימאה הוא בבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: when we say *Atika Stima'a*, that is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שהוא בהעלם הרצון והתענוג לעצמו עדיין,
phrases.en: This is still the hidden *ratzon* and pleasure which is for yourself

phrases.he: רק שחושב להיות הדבר כך בפועל הגילוי
phrases.en: just that you want that you should now be revealed

phrases.he: כמו להיות גילוי הרצון והתענוג להאציל עשר ספירות כו'
phrases.en: that there should be a revealed *ratzon* and *taanug* to bring out the ten *sefiros*
that's why it's called the hidden *taanug*

phrases.he: בחינת העלם לגלוי על כל פנים
phrases.en: it's just like covered, but you know it's really there; it's really able to be revealed and it's meant to be revealed
but the beginning of the *Kav*
is called totally hidden

phrases.he: דגם מחשבה דאדם קדמון לא תפיס ביה כו')
phrases.en: that even the *machshava* of *Adam Kadmon* cannot *tofes* it
that He wants to actually have it: to have the revealed *ratzon* and *taanug* for the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, and the revealed *ratzon* and *taanug* for *Beriya* and for *Yetzira* and *Asiya* also

blocks.text: **When we say Atika Stima'a, that is the Keser of Adam Kadmon.** *Stima'a*, hidden, always means as it is in *Keser* but already come into a *machshava*, associated with something, which is a thing of *bina* (understanding), like the *machshava stima'a* and *mocha stima'a* discussed later.

blocks.text: That is like the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, called the world of *Beriya*, connected with *machshava*. As the *igul* above it, it is *Atika d'Atikin*; *mislabesh* in the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, it is *Atika Stima'a*, hidden within. The general *ratzon* to express yourself already drives particular *ratzonos*, but the hidden *ratzon* behind them is still only to reveal your *ratzon hamuchlat*.

blocks.text: **This is still the hidden ratzon and pleasure which is for yourself, just that you want that you should now be revealed.** You do not really want the house; you want to feel a certain way, and now you want it to actually happen. The *ratzon hamuchlat* alone means: in theory I like things that way, but right now I'm not interested.

blocks.title: Your favorite ice cream
blocks.text: Your favorite ice cream, your favorite song or style of music, does not mean you are in the mood for it right now. It is just in theory.

blocks.title: Interviewing G-d
blocks.text: Say someone interviewed G-d: if You made a world, how would You like it? Would You enjoy being king of a universe? He would answer that He would love it, and want it like this and like that. G-d was daydreaming about it, but did not actually want to do it.

At the time, He was busy "playing with His train set," or chess. Not *kavod* (dignified)? Why must G-d be a sophisticated guy? In this *hishtalshelus* He is the King and chose to reveal Himself in big things, in a dignified way; in another He could do little things. G-d has no parents to tell Him not to play with the trains.

sensitivity.reason: A playful picture of G-d playing with a train set and chess, with no parents to tell Him it is undignified; a reader may take it as irreverent.
sensitivity.publishable: It would not be *kavod* (dignified) in this *hishtalshelus*, where He is the King and chose to reveal Himself in big things, in a dignified way; in another He could do little things. Nothing outside Him tells Him what is fitting.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: NOTES.md calls G-d with His train set borderline. The picture is playful and carries the point (in another *hishtalshelus* He could reveal Himself in little things); weigh whether it reads as irreverent in print or can stand.

blocks.text: So **that there should be a revealed ratzon and taanug to bring out the ten sefiros**: **that's why it's called the hidden taanug**, *Atika Stima'a*, hidden in relation to being revealed: **it's just like covered, but you know it's really there**, meant to be revealed.

**But the beginning of the Kav is called totally hidden**, *stima d'chol stimin*, **that even the machshava of Adam Kadmon cannot tofes** (grasp) **it**, while *Atika Stima'a* is the *taanug* already *mislabesh* in that *machshava*. *Stima* is always the thought of the *ratzon*, not of the intellect: association, as when you know a language and an idea goes with a sound before you think.
So it is still hidden; only He thought **that He wants to actually have it: to have the revealed ratzon and taanug for the sefiros of Atzilus**, and for *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* too.

phrases.en: *Atika Kadisha*, though, is the *taanug* that is in the *chachma* already

phrases.he: והוא בחינת עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: the *taanug* and the *ratzon* of *Atzilus*

like we'll explain everything in detail

blocks.text:
**Atika Kadisha, though, is the taanug that is in the chachma already**, a delight already coming in a particular form. It is *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* of *Atzilus*, **the taanug and the ratzon of Atzilus**: **that's already a revealed ratzon.**

The original *ratzon*, *Atika d'Atikin*, is the inner delight in yourself. Through *Adam Kadmon* it becomes tied to a form, and you delight that it be *davka* this form, because once chosen it will reveal you. That is *Atika Kadisha*: holy, but already connected. **We'll explain everything in detail.**

So far: even the *ratzon kadum*, the first *gilui* after the *Kav*, is still hidden and only for yourself, and so are the *igulim* until *yosher*; the world has not been thought of yet. You know you want to reveal something in the world, but not yet what that means: the *ratzon* for a home before it is a *ratzon* for a house. You do not want a building yet; you want to feel at home.

People sometimes have such desires without knowing what they are, especially Jewish people, but even *goyim*: they feel they are not using their potential, that life is empty and something is missing. They want to feel fulfilled but do not know what will do it, because the *ratzon* is still *b'helem* (hidden). Until they figure it out, it can drive them to try all kinds of weird things.

sections.title: Circles: each cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *igulim* are a wheel inside a wheel: every cause surrounds its effect, and the effect reaches it only from far away, as the reasons a kid makes up never capture why he wants a bike. Each circle starts as one undivided point, a bias, down to the *sof maaseh*, the final deed, which in the circles is the flimsiest and innermost; so too the *ratzon kadum* is ten circles, from the will for a *dira b'tachtonim* to the will for this exact world.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים זה תחת זה הוא כידוע,

that every cause surrounds its effect
And the effect does not grasp, it doesn't reach its cause

blocks.text: **The ten sefiros of igulim, one under the other**: what does it mean that they are a circle inside a circle? As is known, **every cause surrounds its effect. And the effect does not grasp, it doesn't reach its cause**, its source, except **only in a very far away, very far from it, like a wheel inside of a wheel.**

blocks.title: A wheel inside a wheel
blocks.text: A wheel inside a wheel: there is the inner source, the thing you really want, like the inner desire for the house, and the lower thing that comes out of it, the way you will get it. That never fully gives you what you want; the source stays higher.
The quote is from Ezekiel's vision of the Divine chariot, where the *Ofanim* (a class of angels) look like a wheel inside a wheel, with eyes all over. What we mean is concentric circles.

blocks.title: Ripples in a pond
blocks.text: Concentric circles share one center, bigger and bigger, like ripples in a pond, except that here it goes from the outside in: first the outer circle, then each inner one. A pebble dropped in a pond starts from the middle, though even there the biggest ripple goes out first and smaller ones fill in inside it as it grows.

In the Ramak's *hishtalshelus*, which speaks of it from the *reshimu*, the *igulim* do start from the middle and go out. We are speaking of the Arizal's, already set up with the light passing through, so it comes from the top of the circle and goes in.

**Even though the ratzon includes ten**, **it has intellect and emotions**: the *chachma* (wisdom) is the inner goal, and the emotions follow from it, this is good and this is bad. But **it starts off just as one thing; you don't see any divisions in it yet. This is called the circle of a general ratzon**, encompassing all inside it, **which comes specifically from its force**, **but it comes in a far-off way.**

blocks.text: **Like the reason and the intellect for the ratzon, which is called its effect: it's impossible for it to be close to its source, its cause, which is the desire**, because there is no reason for a *ratzon* at all, **as is known.**

blocks.title: A kid who wants a bike
blocks.text: A kid wants a bike, *nekuda* (period), as they say in Hebrew. At this level there is no reason: he wants it because he wants it. Once he has decided, he makes up reasons, excuses for his parents: he will get to school faster, it is healthy. The reasons are invented because of his *ratzon*; they do not make it. His *ratzon* is the cause and they are its effect.

blocks.title: A kid who wants a bike
blocks.text: Nor do they capture the *ratzon*, so they are not the real reason. Tell him he can walk to school, and he needs to be there on time; tell him he can run, get exercise and arrive on time, and the reason is gone but he still wants the bike.

blocks.title: Helping shlep the couch
blocks.text: People often will not say outright what they want, so they give a side reason, to make it look like a rule when there is only what they want. Asked to help *shlep* a couch, they would love to, but... They just do not want to, so they find an excuse. A reason takes it off yourself: it is not that you do not want to; something else stops you.

blocks.title: Helping shlep the couch
blocks.text: But then you can be cornered, since your reason can be disproved: someone else will take care of your errand, so now you can help, and look what you got yourself into. The reason never captures the *ratzon*.

blocks.title: A belief and its proofs
blocks.text:
The same with a belief. Say people believe the Rebbe is *Moshiach*. Asked why, they cite this *sicha* (talk), this Rambam. That does not mean it is not true, but they believe it because they believe it, not because of the proofs: disprove them and they will not give in; they will find another, because the intellect comes from the *ratzon*.

That is *chachma* to *bina*: the *igul* (circle) of the *chachma* forces the *igul* of the *bina* to prove it, but the proofs never capture the *chachma*. And the inner *ratzon* is for the Rebbe, that they want the Rebbe to be *Moshiach*.

sensitivity.reason: Uses those in Chabad who hold that the Rebbe is Moshiach as the example of a belief held regardless of proof, a live and divisive question within the movement.

That is *chachma* to *bina*: the *igul* (circle) of the *chachma* forces the *igul* of the *bina* to prove it, but the proofs never capture the *chachma*, and behind it is the inner *ratzon*.

blocks.text: Again: **it's impossible for it to be close to its source, its cause**, the *ratzon*, because **there's no reason for ratzon whatsoever**, **and it will never reach it.** The intellect never really captures the *ratzon*.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless, the chachma is coming from the ratzon**, and it too is **without a recognizable division into ten**: just a *nekuda* (point), a bias. Your *ratzon* does not hand you a particular *chachma*; it makes your *sechel* (intellect) lean a certain way, so whenever you reach a particular reasoning, it finds something that fits.

blocks.title: A bias toward kindness
blocks.text: Say your *ratzon* leans toward *chesed* (kindness). Then your intellect leans that way and you are liberal-minded, whether toward your son, always seeing him favorably, or in general, liberal or conservative, in politics or anything. It is a leaning, not yet a reasoning: you look for reasons and a worldview that fit how you want things to turn out. Yet the *sechel* never captures the *ratzon*; it only brings it out.

**This is like a bribe** (*shochad*): **the bribe makes you find the reason for the ratzon.** Someone bribed a judge over a case: he has no reason yet why the man is innocent, but now he will always look at things with that bias.

**And even though this reason also includes ten**, *ratzon*, *sechel* and *middos*, a whole world of finding a reason and proving it, it comes as a general thing: **right now you didn't develop and reveal all those pratim** (details); **right now it's just the point, the bias.**

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה לא ישיגנו העיגול דבינה שנעשה מכחו,
phrases.en: and so too the *bina* doesn't reach the *chachma*

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה המדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה
phrases.en: and so too with each emotion, one after the other, until it comes to *sof maaseh*
which is the last thing

phrases.he: והכל ברצונו לעצמו כלול הכל עד סוף מעשה
phrases.en: and all this is all in the desire for himself, which includes everything, till the final action
which is the innermost thing of everything

blocks.text: **And so too the bina doesn't reach the chachma.** The claim, view or belief is the *chachma*, the proofs brought for it the *bina*, and they do not meet: the proofs do not really prove it, and cannot really change it.
This is more *b'gilui* in alternative things, pseudo-sciences, New Age spirituality, cultish-type things: very little reasoning, one little proof with everything piled on it.

sensitivity.reason: A dismissive remark about New Age spirituality, pseudo-sciences and "cultish-type things".
sensitivity.publishable: This is more *b'gilui* where a view has very little reasoning: one little proof with everything piled on it.

blocks.text: **And so too with each emotion, one after the other**: it comes out that a thing is good and to be liked, **until it comes to sof maaseh** (the final action), **which is the last thing**, in a way the most fake and the most flimsy.

It is not even an actual thing, only a daydream of things being a certain way; it will not really happen and will never give you what you want. By the time it gets down to action, the inner desire, to be rich, to have a home that expresses your taste, comes out in such little things that it hardly captures what you want.

blocks.title: A kid in a bakery with two bucks
blocks.text: Such limited self-expression is why kids in a bakery cannot decide: in your imagination you want so many things, and all you have is two bucks. Even with money for any one thing, you walk away with one. So in life: you can do one thing, and it has to express all your emotions, your taste, your whole worldview and inner desire, "and you know, it's like nothing."

**And all this is all in the desire for himself, which includes everything, till the final action.** Even the last *igul* is not the details of how he will do it, only the bias, the *nekuda*, the decision to do this; how, he has not worked out, **which is the innermost thing of everything.**

and it includes ten *sefiros*

phrases.en: in a way of a circle inside of a circle, until the circle of the *sof maaseh*

blocks.text: So it is in the hidden will, surrounded by all the other *igulim*. The biggest thing is the inner *ratzon*, say for a home. That makes a *chachma*, a picture; then a *bina* justifies and explains it and makes distinctions, what brings it closer and what takes it farther. Once it is divided into parts, there can be *middos*.

blocks.question: Why can't you have middos from a chachma?
blocks.text: Because in *chachma* it is all or nothing: it is or it is not, so how could you like it more or less? With *middos* from *bina* you see many parts, and can be excited that it is getting closer.

You like this a little more and that a little less, and you work on it until it is built your way: the *middos* are how you react, change and measure things out. Making a house, how big to make the kitchen and the other rooms, the *middos* down to the physical dimensions, comes from an understanding in *bina* of the picture in *chachma* of what you want in *Keser*.

You want to express your taste; once you picture what expresses it, you can work out its parts, draw plans and details. The details come out in the *middos*, and the *middos* in the *sof maaseh*, where you actually buy the house.

You could design more than one house that fits your *middos*, and you pick one; ask why, and the answer is only that you want that one. That too is a *nekuda*: you make up your mind, and now it expresses your inner *ratzon*. So it is the innermost, existing only within the rest: you want this house for these *middos*, and care about them only within this *bina* and *chachma*.

blocks.title: Dressing in style
blocks.text: Someone wants to dress in style and buys a certain thing. Why? For its shapes and colors, which are *middos*. Why care about those? Because in *bina* he associates them with being in style. The *chachma* is his picture of what being in style means, different for different groups; the inner *ratzon* is to be in style, or to express himself, depending how far in you go. The thing exists only within all that surrounds it, so it is called the *pnimi* (innermost).

**This is the ratzon hane'elam, which is called the ratzon kadum, the source of all the ratzonos, and it includes ten sefiros.** **So too** G-d's first *ratzon* for the whole world: one general circle holding all ten, **in a way of a circle inside of a circle, until the circle of the sof maaseh.**

First the *ratzon* for a *dira b'tachtonim*, the most general; then that it have a certain form, the inner thing of *Atzilus*; then that the form be tied to certain things; then certain *middos*; until a certain *sof maaseh*, the final *igul*: G-d wants this world exactly as it is. On the level of the *middos*, infinite worlds could still meet the specifications.

And **the first circle that includes everything**, is the *ratzon kadum*. Everything exists only within it: G-d wants anything, at least in the *hishtalshelus* as He set it up, only as part of the *dira b'tachtonim*. Nothing means anything without it, and nothing alone reaches it. So the *gilui* in *Atzilus* does not truly express it; He chose that it pass through there, but it does not capture it.

blocks.title: Giving flowers
blocks.text: You have to read between the lines, since nothing captures it. Giving flowers expresses nothing, such a little thing. The *etzem* (essence) stays a *makif* (encompassing light) over it and comes into no *kli* (vessel); you see from the context what it expresses, but it is only a sign, a token.

blocks.title: The strings of the tallis
blocks.text: That is the idea of *tzitzis*: the *tallis* stands for a big *makif* around everything, and to carry it to the next level there are strings that come out, a token of it.

**Until the circle of the sof maaseh**, the *ratzon* for the final deed: **that Hashem wanted to actually do everything that He wanted, to actually make the world.** And **the first circle that includes everything**, is the *ratzon kadum* mentioned above.

So it goes with the *igulim*: first the *ratzon kadum*, the original desire for the *dira b'tachtonim*, the seventh millennium, down to the *ratzon* for the exact form of the world and every last hair on your head. Once that picture, the whole of history, was decided, G-d decided to do it *b'poel mamash*: the last circle.

sections.title: Yosher: once you decide to do it, the order turns over and the deed is on top
sections.summary: When the will for oneself comes to be done in actual fact, everything reverses: the *ratzon* hides in the intellect, the intellect in the *middos*, and the *middos* in the deed, until the *sof maaseh*, which in the circles was a daydream, becomes the king that everything must fit. *Igulim* are the dream and the passion, *teshuva*; *yosher* is the practical, the good deeds, where the bottom line is whether you do it.

phrases.he: וכשבא הרצון לעצמו הזה להיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: and when this *ratzon* for Himself comes, that He actually wants to do it
it's the opposite

blocks.title: Dreaming of a home
blocks.text: **And when this ratzon for Himself comes, that He actually wants to do it**, it is the opposite. Say a man wants a home, his own space. He dreams of his dream house, what he thinks is cool, builds a whole picture, even looks at houses, but he is not serious; it is all dreaming. Then, once he has worked out clearly enough what he wants, he decides to actually do it, and his whole perspective changes: he stops dreaming and starts doing.

His focus turns around. Until now the main thing was what he wants, and everything had to stay transparent to that; he could choose anything, as kids are told they can be whatever they want to be. In *igulim* the biggest thing, which surrounds and defines everything, is what you want. When you actually want to do it, the focus changes.

blocks.title: The Frierdiker Rebbe's plan on the boat
blocks.text: On the boat to America the Frierdiker Rebbe (the Previous Rebbe) dictated to his secretary his plan for America: *Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch*, *Kehos* and *Machane Israel*. Why not wait until he arrived and saw the situation? Because once there he would be influenced by what he saw, and his plan would be an American Judaism; he wanted a European Judaism, "an uncompromised ideal of the way things should be."

There are always two steps. First you set a goal without considering the outside world: if everything went as you dream, what is your ideal? There the top circle has to be what you want, what would really make you happy, and everything else is flexible, transparent to it.

blocks.title: I need a million dollars? I'll get a job
blocks.text: Then, when you decide to actually do it, the dream you picked becomes the top priority, and everything has to fit within it. It has to look exactly like that; it is not up for compromise. It will be hard, cost money and time; you do not care. "I need a million dollars? Okay, I'll get a job then," or a loan, or ask your parents. You figure out how.

So when you do it *b'poel mamash*, everything is defined the opposite way: the *sof maaseh* becomes king of everything, not flexible at all, and defines the rest. That is the difference between *igulim* and *yosher*: actually wanting to do it is the ten *sefiros* of *yosher*, where the *maaseh* (deed) is at the top.

blocks.title: Getting the pizza
blocks.text: What are you in the mood for tonight? You think only of what you would really like if everything went perfectly, not whether it can be done: pizza. Then you commit to it, and start figuring it out: get dressed, find wheels, scrape around for cash, or if that fails, make it yourself. If you really want it, you find a way: *ein davar ha'omed bifnei haratzon*, nothing stands in the way of the will.

So with G-d. He planned the *dira b'tachtonim* in *igulim*, everything transparent to His *ratzon*. Once He settled on a form, a *maaseh*, and decided He wants it *b'poel mamash*, that became the top thing, and from then on everything in the *hishtalshelus* follows that *sof maaseh*. It becomes the *Keser*: the *Malchus* of the higher becomes the *Keser* of the lower, the king. If the king tells you to move a mountain, you cannot say no; you find a way, and it happens.

blocks.question: Is this the change from igulim to yosher, or from yosher to igulim?
blocks.text: Either way is possible, but here we go from *igulim* to *yosher*: the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* are done, and now their *Malchus* becomes the top thing, totally set.

But it is not an ordinary case of the higher *Malchus* becoming the lower *Keser*; it is not the same *Malchus*. Your main *ratzon* now is that it actually happen, and you still have to work out what the house will look like. Your focus is on the physical building, not the planning and the *ratzon* behind it; the *ratzon* for the house exists only to get you to get it, since what you really want is the home.

There are two *ratzonos*. The *ratzon* of *yosher* is the lowest, and you do not care about it; the *ratzon* of *igulim* is the highest, that you get the pleasure you want. The pleasure of getting the building is a low means to an end, to get you to make the house: "It's just like a candy, it's a bait."

Whether you enjoy house shopping is what you care about least, and people usually do not enjoy it: it is the flimsiest *ratzon* and *taanug*, made only strong enough to get you going. The intellect counts a little more, since you need it to do it right; the *middos* more, that you feel good about it; and the main thing is that you have the house.

We just finished the *sefiros* of *igulim*, where the top one is the main one and the inside one the least. There you focus on what you want, and whatever represents it is a token that does not reach it, so it is transparent, almost irrelevant: naming something in a language you invent, any name will do, because the main thing is you and what you decide.

blocks.text:
The whole purpose of Elul, Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur is to recognize the *sefiros* of *igulim*, up to the top *igul*: *mesirus nefesh* for G-d Himself, the *Baal HaRatzon* (the One whose will it is). If He told us to chop wood, jump off the roof, or run around screaming like an insane person, we would do it. If He wants eleven *sefiros*, there are eleven. Nature, order, the *dira b'tachtonim* and *gilui Atzmus* are all His invention, and really irrelevant.

So *teshuva* (return) means saying, "I don't care about Shabbos, I don't care about *aveira* (sin), I don't care about Torah and *mitzvos* at all," only about whatever G-d wants of me, nothing as a thing in its own right, not even the *dira b'tachtonim*. That is *teshuva*: reconnecting to the original source, the first *igul*.

blocks.text: From Yom Kippur to Sukkos is going into *yosher*, where it is the opposite. Once you commit to doing whatever G-d wants, the thing He picks takes on the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*: if He says to put on *tefillin* every day, you will die to put them on. Communist Russia could not stop them from *tefillin* or Shabbos, down to shoelaces: told to tie them the way the *goyim* do, "you'll laugh in their face and let them kill you." Even for the smallest *prat* of the *ratzon*, total *mesirus nefesh*.

Once you commit to doing whatever G-d wants, the thing He picks takes on the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*: if He says to put on *tefillin* every day, you will die to put them on. Communist Russia could not stop them from *tefillin* or Shabbos, down to shoelaces: told to tie them the way the non-Jews do, "you'll laugh in their face and let them kill you." Even for the smallest *prat* of the *ratzon*, total *mesirus nefesh*.

blocks.text: To get there you first have to stop caring about the things themselves: that is the *igulim*, where only His *ratzon* matters. Then, when G-d chooses how He wants it *b'poel mamash*, it switches to *yosher*, and the *maaseh* becomes the main thing, done exactly by the outward details of *halacha*. The *kavanos* (intentions) are only ways to get you there: "the main thing is that you do it."

blocks.text: Like the story told last week of the Frierdiker Rebbe coming to America, and of the *shliach* (emissary) going to Johannesburg, "I think." Planning in 770 or on the boat is *igulim*: you plan by what you want, not by what is possible and practical, and everything else is *batel* (nullified) to that. Once you choose one plan *b'poel mamash*, it is fixed, and everything becomes how to get there, even how to make yourself want it. That is a *hachlata* (a decision): you switch, and the *maaseh* becomes the main thing.

blocks.title: A kid in a toy store with a dollar
blocks.text: Planning which house you want, you are flexible, this one or that one. But at some point you have to say that is it, only one, and people often find that jump hard: "It's an immaturity." Kids in a toy store with a dollar want everything, so whatever they finally buy disappoints, because it is not everything else. You have to pick one and keep to it, since every change of goal means starting over; resolve to do it no matter what, and then everything is figuring out how.

blocks.text:
That is why on Sukkos you go into the *sukka*: the *mitzvos* are like a temporary structure. You have to see through it, that you do them only because G-d said so, the *makif* of the *igulim* within the *yosher*; hence the temporary hut and the roof you see through.

So, he likes to tell people, the purpose of Sukkos is to teach that "you're not supposed to be *frum*" (religious). People form a picture of what being *frum* means, make it their goal, and forget that they just want to do whatever G-d wants. All year you have a house, a set structure like a *Shulchan Aruch*, your picture of how to be, kept safe from outside influences. Every now and then you have to step out of the box, do *teshuva* and remember why you do it, that it is flexible. Then you set it again: most of the year it has to be a house.

blocks.text: But you have to start with at least the *kavana* that it is *lishma* (for its own sake). That is why in *halacha* the main thing is to remember *lishma* at the start: that is when you decide, and you must decide because G-d said so. Once decided, you can forget why, since it is now a different *ratzon*, focused on how; you need not hold the *kavana* the whole time.

blocks.text: In *igulim* the focus is on yourself: you want the house because it will make you happy, fulfilled, with your own space. But once this *ratzon* for yourself is to be *b'poel mamash*, once you decide to actually do a certain house, **it's the opposite.**

phrases.en: the *ratzon* becomes hidden
and it goes into *sechel*
and the *sechel* surrounds the *ratzon*, meaning that it's bigger than the *ratzon*

phrases.he: והשכל מתעלם ומתלבש במדות זה תחת זה
phrases.en: then the *sechel* gets hidden and gets put into the *middos*, one under the other

phrases.he: עד סוף מעשה, הוא העליון מהכל

blocks.text: **The ratzon becomes hidden, and it goes into sechel.** Once you want to actually get a house, you put the *ratzon* aside: the main thing is no longer what I want but the *sechel*, which has to tell me what is reasonable to want.

blocks.title: Buckingham Palace for the garage
blocks.text: In *igulim* he would like to live in a great big palace, maybe Buckingham Palace, or use Buckingham Palace for the garage and build a bigger one. Then he comes to do it, reaches into his pocket and finds two nickels and a dime, enough for a cardboard box outside the museum. His intellect tells him to lower his expectations, or get a job, or find something more reasonable, and a way to do it.

Even if he does not lower his desire, in a way he does, because in the *sechel* his picture becomes practical and limited. The way of the *oros d'Tohu* (lights of Chaos) with the *kelim d'Tikun* (vessels of Repair) is not to lower the final goal but to find a practical way that starts leading toward it. Normally, though, people just do *oros d'Tikun* with *kelim d'Tikun*; we are not up to *Tikun* yet, but for now it is almost the same thing.

So the *sechel* becomes the main thing: **and the sechel surrounds the ratzon, meaning that it's bigger than the ratzon**, and the *ratzon* does not reach it. What you want is very nice, but if it does not make sense, too bad. The *sechel* is now more real: it can change the *ratzon*, and the *ratzon* cannot change it. The *sechel* is on top.

**Then the sechel gets hidden and gets put into the middos, one under the other.** It sounds very good on paper, but then the *middos* kick in and tell the *sechel* which plan you will do: in theory you could, but you are scared, or you do not like it. A garbage man can make a lot of money with good benefits, and you still do not want to do that.

blocks.question: Are the middos the same ratzon?
blocks.text: No. *Middos* means the way you relate to something, the way you react. There is a *ratzon* higher than *sechel* and a *ratzon* lower than it, and the lower one is in the *middos*.

blocks.title: I like candy
blocks.text: I like candy: that is my *ratzon*, higher than *sechel*. My *sechel* tells me what will get me candy, that if I behave I get it. The *middos* are how I react when, say, my parents are watching and I can listen or not. "*Ratzon* plus *sechel* equals *midda*": the *sechel* is a function that spins out which *midda* to have. That you now see listening to your parents as good, have a *chesed* toward it and are scared to cross them, since then no candy: those are *middos*. The inner desire is for the candy.

Before, the *sechel* was the bigger circle with the *middos* inside. Now the *sechel* is *metzamtzem* (contracted) and the *middos* go around it; then the *middos* are *metzamtzem* and the *maaseh* goes around them, **the middos one under the other, until the sof maaseh goes on top of everything, the highest one of everything.**

These are two separate *hishtalshelus*'s at once. The *igulim*, a circle inside a circle, go down to the *sof maaseh*. Alongside them, starting after, come the *sefiros* of *yosher*, like a person in three lines, where each higher one is *metzamtzem* and *mislabesh* in the lower one, all the way down.

blocks.title: A swimming pool
blocks.text: In *yosher*, first you work out what you want, like *Atzilus*; then what that means, if you like to swim, a swimming pool; then its exact form, how big and built of what, like *Yetzira*; then how to build it, like *Asiya*. In *igulim* you want all that too, but the lower you go the less you care, since it is not your main *ratzon*. That is why people like to daydream: the circles keep getting smaller and farther from the real thing.

In *igulim* it is all a daydream. Picturing yourself digging out the swimming pool is the most fake, farthest from doing it; the most real thing is that you want it. But once you stop imagining and decide to actually do it, you start actually wanting it, and first you work out what you want.

blocks.title: A swimming pool
blocks.text: Wanting to swim becomes *mislabesh* in the *ratzon* for a swimming pool, and now you want a pool, not to swim. Swimming you could have at a lake or the beach, but you decided to live in the city and have a pool. Once decided, the other *ratzonos* are covered over: all you see is the pool, and hidden inside it is the kernel of truth, that you just want to swim. That kernel is the *igul* of *ratzon*, now *metzamtzem* into the *sechel*.

blocks.title: A swimming pool
blocks.text: Then you look through catalogs and see one pool right for your price range, house and size. Now those *middos*, which also means dimensions, how big, what material, the price, become the main thing, and the general picture of a pool is *metzamtzem* and *mislabesh* in them: you want that one. "That's what catalogs do. They get you to go from wanting a pool to wanting this pool."

He sees it with people all the time. A moment ago they were hungry and in the mood for anything; then their heart is set on one thing, they get excited and forget why they wanted it. If it turns out to be a real pain to get, they cannot switch to something more practical; it becomes a crisis that they cannot have it the exact way they pictured. "It's like a little bit of an *akshanus*," a little stubborn.

Then wanting that specific thing becomes *mislabesh* in a *maaseh*: they decide to work and save, and can get so caught up in the work that they forget why. There is no real *hishtalshelus* in *ratzon*, above all in the *igulim*, where a lower *igul* can blow up into a bigger one. Once a higher stage is tied to a lower one, the lower takes over as the all-encompassing goal, and everything else hides in the background.

blocks.question: Why does yosher look like a person?
blocks.text: There is a *yosher* that does not yet necessarily look like a person. But this is how a person works: the *ratzon* goes into the *sechel*, the *sechel* into the *middos*, the *middos* into the *maaseh*, and it comes out. Going through those human steps, the *ratzon* takes the shape of a person. The *igulim* are the soul before it enters the body; *yosher* is the soul in the body, working the way people work.

In the *igulim* you also go through all the steps, but the *ratzon* stays on top and never becomes *batel* to the *sechel*; the *sechel* is *batel* to it. The *ratzon* bribes the *sechel* to find a fitting reason, so you are biased; the *sechel* bribes the *middos*, and the *middos* bribe the *maaseh*, until you tell yourself you will do "these crazy things" to reach the *middos* you want.

*Yosher* is the opposite. The *igulim* are oriented to passion; *yosher* to the practical, and the top thing becomes the best way to do it. The *maaseh* is the context that defines everything: if a certain way is more practical, you change the *middos*, the exact form of what you wanted, and that changes the *sechel* and the *ratzon*. Since the main goal is to actually do it, everything has to fit what can actually be done. That is what being practical means.

This is *teshuva* and *maasim tovim* (good deeds): *teshuva* is *igulim*, *maasim tovim* is *yosher*. These are the two steps, *ratzo* and *shov* (running and returning), *MaH* and *BaN*, which include everything: the *igulim* are *MaH*, the *yosher* *BaN*.

inside of the *poel mamash* was *machshava*
and inside that is the *middos*

ונמצא פנימי מכולם הוא הרצון והתענוג,

this is *yosher*

phrases.en: when the upper one goes into the lower one

blocks.text: **The final thing, the maaseh b'poel mamash**, includes everything: **inside of the poel mamash was machshava, and inside that is the middos**, in the *middos* *chachma* and *bina*, and in the *chachma* the *ratzon* and *taanug*. So **the most inner, hidden thing is the taanug and the ratzon, and the most external thing, the lowest thing, is the maaseh.** In *yosher* the *maaseh* is on top, the outside you see; in *igulim* what you see is the *ratzon* and *taanug*, and the *maaseh* is only its representation.

"The thought that counts" is the motto of *igulim*: you meant well. *Yosher* answers that the path to hell is paved with good intentions; show me the bottom line, did you do it or not? *Maaseh hu ha'ikar* (the deed is the main thing), never mind the good intentions, show me the buckaroos. The Frierdiker Rebbe says you need cold, hard cash: *kove'a itim l'Torah* (set times for Torah), actually doing things.

In *yosher* the main thing is the whole point of this week's *parsha*: G-d wants you to do *yosher*, and you need not worry about the *igulim*. *Hanistaros la'Hashem Elokeinu v'haniglos lanu ul'vaneinu*: the hidden things, the *igulim*, why He wants it and what He gets from it, are G-d's business; yours is what He told you, do this and this will happen. So *ki karov eilecha hadavar me'od, b'ficha uvilvavcha la'asoso*: He told you black on white in the Torah, and the main thing is doing the *mitzvos*, not the spiritual levels. And whether you did it is very easy to know.

The Torah itself gives only the bottom line, what it wants; the Oral Torah and the Rabbis tell you what to do to get yourself there. The Torah forbids the bad relations, so the Rabbis say to dress and act with *tznius* (modesty); the Torah leaves out those details, since they are not the main *ratzon*, only how to get yourself to do it. Like an employer: "I'm paying you to finish the job"; you are the expert, figure out how, but make it look like this. The behind-the-scenes is theirs; the bottom line is whether you do it.

So it says *Elokim asa es ha'adam yashar*, G-d made man straight, *v'heima bikshu tachbulos*, and they made schemes in *igulim*: G-d told us to do this, but looking into the *igulim* we see what He really wants, so we will do it another way and He will like it even better. They try to improve on what He told them.

Which in a way we are going to do, he adds: that is the *inyan* of *teshuva*, doing something better that G-d did not even ask for. But it is also a source of sin, because we are not listening to Him.

**This is yosher, when the upper one goes into the lower one.**

sections.title: The ratzon kadum goes by circles, and comes from the reshimu through a short line
sections.summary: Because the *ratzon kadum* is still for oneself, it goes by way of circles, its first circle the general *makif* of all the worlds. Before it, the beginning of the *Kav* is a short line, one little point that carries the essence and stands for all of it, as a hair comes from the brain; so from the *reshimu*, still infinite though limited, the *Kav* measures out one little *ratzon kadum*.

And this first igul is the general makif for the entire ABYA.**

is a *hiyuli hamshacha*

blocks.text: **And the reshis hakav**, the little line before this first circle, **is a hiyuli hamshacha** (a raw, general drawing forth), **similar to the little line that connects the ila to the alul**, the cause to the effect.

blocks.title: A hair from the brain
blocks.text: The lower circle does not really reach the upper one; it only represents it. That is the idea of a *kav*, a line, or a hair, wherever the *tzimtzum* of hairs and lines is mentioned: in one small point the *etzem* is carried over, totally *metzumtzam* (contracted), a mere representation. A hair comes from the very stuff of your brain, but it is detached, and you do not see the connection, though there is one. Or a *dugma* (an example): one thing taken to stand for the whole.

That is a line: you pick one little point of the essence and use it as if it were everything. Your *ratzon* could come out any way; you pick one *chachma*, one picture out of infinite pictures, and the connection is a little line. So the whole *ratzon kadum*, the desire for a *dira b'tachtonim*, is a little line from the *Atzmus Ein Sof*: one little example of how the *ratzon hamuchlat* could come out.

In the *ratzon hamuchlat* there is no up and down, only the taste. That it was set up with ten *sefiros* and this as the main priority could have come out in infinite ways, so that too is a little line. The *Kav* is such a line, bringing out a little thing, **like from ratzon to chachma.**

phrases.he: כך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל נמשך קו בצמצום גדול מאד
phrases.en: so too from the *reshimu*, which has hidden in it all of G-d's taste of how He would want anything He would ever want and how He would do anything (the whole *Atzmus Ein Sof* is hidden there), comes out one little *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: דהגם שהרשימו הוא בא בהגבלה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: even though we said that the *reshimu* was very limited, it's already like a *metzumtzam* thing

phrases.he: אבל הוא מבחינת עולם האין סוף על כל פנים,
phrases.en: it's still the world of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: רק שהוא בחינת האחרונה שנעשה בקיצור כו'
phrases.en: It's just like the end of the *Ein Sof*, which is made like in a short way

blocks.text: **So too from the reshimu**, in which is hidden all of G-d's taste, how He would want anything and do anything, the whole *Atzmus Ein Sof*, there comes out **one little ratzon kadum**, a *kav* in a very great contraction.

**Even though we said that the reshimu was very limited**, **it's still the world of the Ein Sof.** "So a zero in the world of the *Ein Sof* is more infinite than an infinity in the world of an *igul*." The *Atzmus Ein Sof* is like someone with a *ratzon hamuchlat*, a taste, already the last level, *Kadmon*: He chose to reveal Himself in a certain way.

But even that particular way, *Kadmon*, is still a taste, totally infinite compared with coming out into the world. In *Kadmon* He picks a taste because He feels Himself in that style. When He is *metzamtzem* it into a *reshimu*, He hides Himself: what is left are the choices of His style and taste, without seeing Him in them. That is the *reshimu*.

Yet all of that is still far more infinite than any particular *hishtalshelus*, like making a house, because there is no up and down yet: you could want the whole house for the bathroom drapes. In the *reshimu* he already knows; ask him how he would want his house and he can tell you. But to actually want a house takes the *tzimtzum* of the *Kav*, which pulls out and measures what comes out and in what order.

The *Kav* measured out that he will want a house as the main thing, with the details and what it takes to get it secondary: his goal is a home, and that automatically includes doing whatever it takes to get one. Then it goes to *yosher*: when he actually decides, he gets a job and works, whatever a home takes.

The *Kav* is *chozer u'meir*: it reveals the light again a little. The *Kav* always means your choice, so it reveals you: you choose which way to bring it out, you measure it, and you see yourself measuring.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: In the *mashal* of the teacher, the *reshimu* is all the knowledge in his memory, facts in a way separate from him: there is him and there are the things he knows. When he is not thinking of them they are there hidden, without his mind showing in them. The *Kav* is his measuring out which students and subjects to teach and which explanations to bring out. Those explanations were measured by him, so there is a kind of *gilui ohr* (revealed light), his mind revealed in them.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 61 opens by going on with the reshimu and the Kav (lines 47-48), with the mashal of the teacher, before it rereads line 48.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: Someone deep in thought, all his understanding in play, makes a *tzimtzum*: he clears his mind and gives the students his full attention. Then he takes out his *kav*, measures the students, and chooses what to bring out and in what order, an idea they will understand. He picks the *meshalim*: tennis for the one who likes tennis, hunting for the hunter, cars for the car guy. Idea for the student's level, *kelim* (vessels) of explanation, *meshalim*, and he puts it all together.

blocks.text: The *Atzmus* is not a desire to do something; it is just being yourself. Deciding to be someone who does something is the *sof maaseh* of the *machshava* of the *Ein Sof*, the end of *Kadmon*: you tie yourself to doing things a certain way, to express yourself. You want to leave an impression of yourself in the world, a *reshimu*. The *tzimtzum* makes a *gilui* separate from you that still reflects on you: that you chose this idea to come out this way reveals you.

blocks.title: A painter's signature
blocks.text: That is your choice: pick a style or a taste, and anything done that way is like a signature. Each painter has his character, and one look tells you who did it. That is a *reshimu*, an imprint left by the person.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 61 opens by going on with the reshimu and the Kav (lines 47-48), with the mashal of the teacher, before it rereads line 48.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: In a teacher, the desire to teach is the desire for a *reshimu*: to leave an impression of your intellect in someone else's mind. So you hide your intellect and reveal the *koach hagvul* (the power of limitation), making it into ideas as if separate from you. Really it is you, since ideas cannot be separated from the one who thought them; but you make them as if separate, and then you can give them over.

blocks.text: Even though the *reshimu* comes in a limited way, it is still of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*: the *koach hagvul* of the *Ein Sof*, and still infinite, every possible limited thing G-d could make that might seem separate, not one *gvul* (limit) but every possible *gvul*. **It's just like the end of the Ein Sof, which is made like in a short way.** But it is still infinite.

**Therefore, it has to come through a short Kav.** To jump from the *reshimu* of the *koach*, at the end of the *Ein Sof*, to the start of the *hishtalshelus*, it has to come as a little *kav*, finite: one little thing picked out to stand for the whole *etzem*.

blocks.question: Is the kav katzar itself the ratzon kadum?
blocks.text: No. The *kav katzar* (the short line) is from chapters 14 and 15; the first *igul* the *Kav* makes is the *ratzon kadum*. For it to come out of the *ratzon hamuchlat* there has to be the *tzimtzum*, which leaves the *reshimu*, and then the *Kav*. The first *igul* has many names: the great *igul*, the *ratzon kadum*, the general *makif* of *Beriya*, sometimes the *machshava kduma* of *Adam Kadmon*, depending on the context.

sections.title: Up and down begin with the Kav; of the Essence above it nothing can be said
sections.summary: The *Kav* only makes an up and a down, taking one little detail of the will and connecting it to *chachma*. In the world of the *Ein Sof* there is no up and down, only simple unity, the way a person's taste is the person; so it cannot be spoken of, and only the *Kav* and *Adam Kadmon*, the cause of all causes, can be grasped. The *tzimtzum* is a jump, not a line, which is why the Essence is called holy, and why *Adam Kadmon* is a man while of the Essence it says, "He is not a man."

It does this by taking one little *prat* of the *ratzon* and tying it to the *chachma*, so the *chachma* stands for just that one *prat* of the *Keser*.

blocks.text: **But in the world of the Ein Sof**, with none of that *Kav* business, **there's not even an up and down.** Even with all the *tzimtzumim* it stays on one level, totally infinite, the *Atzmus* of the *Ein Sof*.

**It's just completely an achdus pshuta** (simple unity), **one simple thing**: the *gilui* of G-d exactly as He is. In a person, it is simply you: your taste is you. Books on style in writing all say the style is the person, not a separate thing.

**Even though He estimated what's going to be**, like a taste, **it's all within yourself.** You were not thinking of the particular things to come; you chose a taste for yourself, which is really you, deciding what kind of person to be. That **is still completely infinite.**

blocks.text: That is why style is so hard to explain. All they can tell you is not to think about it: think of the *sof maaseh*, and it comes out *mimeila* (by itself), because it is you. Try to bring it out, and you cover it with a *kelipa* (a husk).

blocks.text: **But Atzmus Ein Sof, no thought can grasp it**, not even the *machshava kduma*, the first thought of the *ratzon kadum*. **The Ein Sof is totally separate. It's called completely kadosh** (holy). Why *kadosh*? **Because of the tzimtzum.**

So no *kav* connects them: from before the *tzimtzum* to after it is a jump, not a line. Everywhere else He picks one little part of what He wants to reveal and makes it like everything: one swimming pool, one shape, one material, a little of the *etzem*. In the first *tzimtzum* everything was hidden: "You went from being you to being something outside of you, and that's it." You hid yourself; you did not pick a little piece of yourself.

blocks.text: But **the ratzon kadum is called His great name**: *shmo* (His name) has the *gematria* (numerical value) of *ratzon*, **in other words, it's His big desire.** And this is the meaning of *Yehei shmei rabba mevarach*.

Answering *Yehei shmei rabba mevarach* with the proper *kavana* tears up decrees of seventy years. The *kavana* is that G-d's great name be drawn down into the world, and His great name is the *ratzon* for the *dira b'tachtonim*, for *Moshiach*. So connecting to that *ratzon*, the spreading of the wellsprings, tears up all decrees, because that is the main goal.

blocks.text: As is known, **Adam Kadmon is called Adam d'Beriya**, as will be explained. **But about Atzmus Ein Sof it says ki lo adam hu: it's not a person.** As is known from the *kavanos* of *Nishmas Kol Chai*, **Adam Kadmon is already like a thing of a person, and it's like the soul of creation**; above it nothing can be called a person, since that was a total jump.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between *igulim* and *yosher*, and how does drawing the circles without lifting the pen show what the beginning of the *Kav* does?
In what sense is the *ratzon kadum* already revealed, and in what sense is it still hidden? What do the teenager whose parents cramp his style and the song in your head show?
Why does every last detail, the bathroom drapes or a blade of grass, matter to the first will, and in what way is the last deed first in thought?
Why can the reasons never reach the will? Explain with the kid who wants a bike and with the bribe.
What changes when the will for oneself comes to be done in actual fact, and why does the *sof maaseh* go from the flimsiest circle to the top?
Why can even *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* not be spoken of, and why is the *tzimtzum* called a jump and not a line?
